description:
Two related kit-completeness gaps emerging from this review:

(1) src/permissions.rs declares MANAGE_SPACE, MANAGE_ROLES, MANAGE_MEMBERS, MANAGE_CHANNELS. The spec lists more: ban (used by SpaceBan/set per draft line 1314), manage_emoji (referenced in the may_set_custom_emoji doc — but not actually defined here). When permission enforcement lands for those other ops, the constants need to live here for consistency, and required_permissions_for_op needs to map them.

(2) SpaceInvite is registered with get/changes/set in lib.rs:242-250, but draft §SpaceInvite Methods (lines 1280-1298) does not actually define /query or /queryChanges — confirmed correct. SpaceBan is registered with get/changes/set in lib.rs:253-261, same coverage. These look right.

But: PresenceStatus is registered with get/changes/set (lib.rs:281-289). Per spec §PresenceStatus (if it exists), is /query supported? Need to check whether the kit's coverage matches the spec — this review didn't surface the answer.

The maintainer burden lens: the kit's lib.rs is the canonical registration surface. There's no compile-time check that 'every method the spec defines is registered' (and only those). A future spec edit that adds a method (e.g. SpaceInvite/redeem) would land in the spec, no one would notice, and the kit silently lacks the handler until someone discovers via integration test or end-user complaint.

Mitigation: add a spec-driven test that walks a canonical list of (type, method) tuples from draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 and asserts dispatcher.has_handler(method_name) for each. The list lives in tests/spec_method_coverage.rs and is updated when the spec is updated. A future spec audit bead would file beads for each new (type, method) tuple that comes in.
title: Spec compliance: SpaceInvite & SpaceBan have NO query/queryChanges; permissions module has no BAN constant — extension surface is incomplete
